newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Rally keeps equities busy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Rally keeps equities busy.

text.p: A shortened trading session did not lessen investors' penchant for individual equity options as the broad stock market rallied into new territory Thursday.
"The rally is bringing in a lot of people that might otherwise be at the beach and keeping them glued to screens," said Jon Najarian, president of Mercury Trading, an options trading firm in Chicago.
The Dow industrial average finished the session 100 points higher at a record 7,895.81, its first close above 7,800 after several failed attempts over the last few weeks.
Other market measures also closed in record ground.

Thursday's rally was touched off by a weaker than expected U.S. employment report for June and followed a strong late-session surge Wednesday after the Federal Reserve's policy-setting arm ended its policy meeting with rates unchanged.
A rally in bonds also helped, analysts said.
Najarian said technology stocks were among the leaders on Wednesday and some interest rate-sensitive financial issues were leaders Thursday.

Options on technology stocks remained among the favorites, led by such names as Compaq Computer Corp on the Pacific Exchagne and International Business Machines Corp at the Chicago Board Options Exchange.
Some busy financial stock options included American Express Co and Washington Mutual Inc at the American Stock Exchange.
Options activity was not particularly heavy in shares of Lockheed Martin Corp and Northrop Grumman Corp after the two companies said they agreed to combine in an $11.6 billion deal.
Lockheed shares fell five to 99 and Northrop surged 21 to 109-7/8.
